note: chrome://settings/content/all -- the per-origin site-data list. Chrome's own chrome plus one row per visited origin. KNOWN RESIDUAL, accepted deliberately: those origin strings name sites the browser has visited, so an attacker who gets the browser to their host puts their hostname on this page. A hostname is DNS-charset, no whitespace and 63 characters per label -- capacity-bound in the sense capacity.py already uses -- and masking the rows would break the only thing task 7b6c7e24 does here, which is find amazon.com in this list and delete its data.
